purpose: Record the explicit Bella requirement to preserve the current Compression system and its integration boundary.
status: Approved preservation requirement; no runtime implementation or cutover.
userDirection: Next, Compression: keep the current system as it is. It works and I love it.
preserve: Current codec identification and exact catalogue mappings, qualified format-specific refinements and fallbacks.
Current readable codec names, DNx branding and exact supported older numbered aliases, qualified DNxUncompressed descriptions and companion audio encoding names.
Existing output/consumer behavior and table/CSV presentation, including current source preference when multiple eligible Compression results have already been read.
Existing useful tests and representative fixtures as preservation checks; no naming tests rerun on this documentation-only turn.

integration.reusableCore: Value-only resolver and existing catalogue/DNx rules; no file reading, ParsedSource, AvidObject or scanner evidence graph dependency.
integration.newBellaBoundary: New independent parsers provide equivalent validated format facts through a small adapter later. Keep the resolver/catalogue rules unchanged.
integration.companionBehavior: Preserve the existing WAV/AIFF Summary encoding labels, structured coding-ID normalization, qualified legacy FourCC/resolution recovery with genuine coding absence, exact naming-only clock spelling, geometry/layout/depth/subsampling and alpha/representation qualifications.
integration.numericDepthCompatibility: The existing resolver accepts depth/representation strings. Bella can generate those temporary arguments from numeric depth/format data without storing a formatted Bit Depth label in each result row.
integration.separateTiming: Preserve existing naming-only rate qualifications; the separate Duration interpreter must not silently replace or broaden them.
integration.separateScheduling: This preserves current Compression selection for already-read eligible sources; conditions for opening extra media files remain in the later scanner/header review.
integration.noNewColumns: Preserve current outputs/consumers and prior compact-retention decisions, without adding new visible naming columns.

sourceReceipts.scope: CompressionFacts / CompressionNames contract; pure resolver boundary.
Existing exact codec catalogue and name builder.
MDB qualified inputs, legacy naming clock rules, audio-summary encoding labels.
OMF/native audio qualified inputs and companion labels.
Current Compression/name-source preference for already-read eligible observations.
Existing naming cases to preserve; not rerun for this decision.

relatedBitDepthApproval.reuse: Carry over verified interpretation rules and useful test cases into small new Bella helpers.
relatedBitDepthApproval.storage: Keep depth as a number with necessary format information.
relatedBitDepthApproval.boundary: Independent C++17/Qt 6.5.3 Bella implementation; no wholesale import of OldScanner projection/evidence machinery.
relatedBitDepthApproval.remainingCoverage: Palette/mixed/unsupported RGBA and uncommon fixed-point label details remain as marked for review; the approval does not silently settle every previously proposed edge case.
relatedBitDepthApproval.compression: Separate user decision on the same turn preserves the current Compression system; see mdb-compression-2026-10-20.json.

limits: This is source-boundary inspection and an approved preservation decision, not a new binary reverse-engineering or actual-file codec survey.
No runtime source edits, tests, builds, app cutover, commits or measured speed/memory claims.
Uncommon generic Bit Depth label details still marked for review must not silently alter preserved Compression descriptions.
OldScanner remains active; Bella requirements review continues; Bin Filter unchanged.
